svg.text: S13 · Strain-gauge bridge
Measure a small imbalance
Post-16 · ages 16–19
A small resistance change unbalances the bridge. Its two sense voltages
are nearly equal, so a difference amplifier helps reveal the small signal.
Your investigation
Calculate both bridge midpoint voltages. Predict the amplifier output, then
change Arm1 above and below 1000 ohms. Keep the two sense
connections separate.
This activity
Model the bridge resistors and sweep a small declared resistance
change. Measure differential output and the effect of an initially
unbalanced bridge. Mechanical strain is not generated by the solver.
Getting started
Open the Simulation tab and press Run. Select a source or component to
see its values. Read the labelled signals, then change one quantity at a
time. Equal net labels identify connected points.
Arm1 = 1001 ohms; the other bridge arms = 1000 ohms. Both sense
terminals are free to move. The matched resistor ratios give OUT = 10 ×
(PLUS − MINUS).
Explain:
Use an equation, a truth table or a state sequence to justify your
prediction. Include units and discuss the model assumptions.
The model predicts electrical behaviour; it does not replace real practical
measurements.
